exceptions.title: warns without relying on React owner-stack support
exceptions.reason: The case mocks `SafeReact.captureOwnerStack`, which only React has. The warning of `Drawer.Popup` has no owner stack.

exceptions.title: releases closed drawers once they are removed
exceptions.reason: The case forces a garbage collection through `node:v8`, so Base UI runs it only in jsdom. A browser has no `node:v8`. The case is in the test file that the Node project runs, with the same title. It reads the context of the provider from a server render.

exceptions.title: works before a generated swipe area id is available
exceptions.reason: The case mocks `useId` to give `undefined` at first, as in React 17. `useVaseUiId` gives an id in `setup`, so the swipe area has its id in its first render.

exceptions.title: registers the swipe area once a generated id becomes available
exceptions.reason: The case mocks `useId` to give `undefined` at first, as in React 17. `useVaseUiId` gives an id in `setup`, so the swipe area has its id in its first render.

surfaceAdditions.reason: The part gives `disabled` to `Dialog.Trigger`, which reads it for its state and for `useButton`, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the trigger, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

The part reads `id` to register the swipe area as a trigger in the store of the drawer, and follows a change of it, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the swipe area, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

`Drawer.Title` is `Dialog.Title`. The part gives `id` to the root for `aria-labelledby` and follows a change of it, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the title, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

`Drawer.Description` is `Dialog.Description`. The part gives `id` to the root for `aria-describedby` and follows a change of it, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the description, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

`Drawer.Close` is `Dialog.Close`. The part reads `disabled` for its state and for `useButton`, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the button, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

returnTypeDifferences.reason: `Drawer.Handle` is the class `DrawerHandle`. The declaration of the function names the class, and Base UI documents the same class by its name in the namespace.
